content.content:
# Redmine code and test conventions (as found in 6.1.2)

Canonical reference for the implementer and the reviewer. Everything here was read
from the 6.1.2 tree or the official wiki on 2026-09-07; file pointers are given so it
can be re-verified. Where Redmine has no written rule, the convention is "do what the
surrounding code does", and the pointers show what that is.

## Sources

- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: development happens on redmine.org, not GitHub. Patches must
  include tests and all existing tests must pass.
- Wiki "Coding Standards" (redmine.org/projects/redmine/wiki/Coding_Standards):
  "Make sure any new code is tested, especially in the Controllers and Models. Code
  without tests may (and probably will) be rejected on that reason alone." Prefer
  `blank?`/`present?` over `empty?`/`nil?` in views. Document methods as needed and
  explain any complex code. Otherwise follow the Rails contributing conventions.
- `.rubocop.yml` + `.rubocop_todo.yml`: enforced in CI (`.github/workflows/linters.yml`
  runs `bundle exec rubocop --parallel`). Also `bundle audit` and stylelint on CSS.
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml`: the suite runs on Ruby 3.2/3.3/3.4 against
  PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite. Anything we write must be portable across all three.
- `doc/RUNNING_TESTS`, `lib/tasks/testing.rake`.

## Ruby source files

- **Every Ruby file starts with** `# frozen_string_literal: true`, a blank line, then
  the GPL header exactly as in `app/models/token.rb:1-18`. Migrations are the
  exception: `# frozen_string_literal: true` only (see `db/migrate/20250611092227_enable_pkce.rb`).
- **Hash syntax:** Redmine overwhelmingly uses the rocket style `:key => value`
  (about 2300 occurrences in `app/` versus a handful of `key: value`). Use rockets in
  app code and tests to match neighbors. Migrations and newer files use `key: value`;
  match the file you are in.
- **Style is RuboCop-enforced** with Redmine's own exceptions: metrics cops are
  disabled (`Metrics: Enabled: false`), spacing inside braces is free
  (`Layout/SpaceInsideBlockBraces`, `SpaceInsideHashLiteralBraces` disabled), line
  length has allowances for test names. Do not fight `.rubocop_todo.yml` in files we
  touch; do not add new offenses. Run before every commit:
  `docker compose exec app bundle exec rubocop <changed files>`.
- Target Ruby 3.2 (`TargetRubyVersion: 3.2`): no syntax newer than 3.2.
- Naming: models singular CamelCase in `app/models/`, controllers plural
  `XxxController` in `app/controllers/`, tests mirror the path under `test/`.

## Models

- Inherit from `ApplicationRecord`. Look at `app/models/token.rb` for the size and
  shape of a small model.
- **Mass assignment goes through `safe_attributes`**, Redmine's own mechanism, not
  strong parameters (`app/models/user.rb:819-845`; module in
  `lib/redmine/safe_attributes.rb`). Controllers assign with
  `record.safe_attributes = params[:record]`.
- Access control is `User#allowed_to?` and `Redmine::AccessControl`
  (`lib/redmine/access_control.rb`), not custom checks.
- `User.current` is the request-scoped current user; it is set by the controller.
- Validations use ActiveRecord; error messages come from i18n keys.

## Controllers

- Inherit from `ApplicationController`. Auth filters are declarative:
  `before_action :require_login` (`app/controllers/my_controller.rb:22`),
  `before_action :require_admin` (`app/controllers/settings_controller.rb:27`),
  `require_sudo_mode :action_a, :action_b` (`my_controller.rb:28-29`) for sensitive
  actions. `accept_api_auth :index, :show` declares which actions accept API keys.
- Success flows set `flash[:notice] = l(:notice_...)` and `redirect_to`. Failure
  re-renders the form. See `my_controller.rb:50-75`.
- Routes are explicit in `config/routes.rb` (`my/*` block at line 92). Use `:as` to
  name routes so views can use `xxx_path` helpers; never hardcode URLs in views.
- API responses use `respond_to` with `format.api` and the `.api.rsb` builder views
  (`app/views/my/account.api.rsb`).

## Views (ERB)

- Plain ERB, no other templating. Every user-visible string is `l(:key)` from
  `config/locales/en.yml`. Never a literal English string in a view.
- List pages follow `app/views/auth_sources/index.html.erb`: a `div.contextual` with
  the add link, `<%= title l(:label_xxx_plural) %>`, `<table class="list">` with
  `thead`/`tbody`, rows with `id="record-<id>"`, a `td.buttons` cell using
  `delete_link` (`app/helpers/application_helper.rb:1600`) and `sprite_icon`
  (`app/helpers/icons_helper.rb:36`).
- Sidebars use `content_for :sidebar` (`app/views/my/account.html.erb:75`); page
  titles use `html_title` (line 79). `app/views/my/_sidebar.html.erb` is a partial
  (leading underscore).
- Forms use `labelled_form_for` / `form_tag` with `f.text_field` etc.; look at
  `app/views/my/password.html.erb` for a small form.
- New CSS goes in `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css` and must pass stylelint
  (`.stylelintrc`). Prefer reusing existing classes.
- JavaScript: Stimulus controllers exist (`data-controller="api-key-copy"` in
  `_sidebar.html.erb:23`), plus jQuery. Only add JS if the spec needs it.

## i18n

- Add keys only to `config/locales/en.yml`. Do not touch the other 49 locale files;
  `rake locales:update` propagates English keys to them and maintainers do that.
- Key prefixes: `label_` (nouns, page titles), `field_` (attribute names, used by
  ActiveRecord error messages via `activerecord` mapping too), `button_` (actions),
  `text_` (sentences, help text), `notice_` (flash success), `error_` (flash/validation
  failures), `setting_` (admin settings labels). Plurals are `label_xxx_plural`.
- Run `docker compose exec app bin/rails locales:check_interpolation` if a key uses
  `%{placeholders}`.

## Settings

- Declared in `config/settings.yml` with a default; accessed as `Setting.xxx` /
  `Setting.xxx?`; rendered in admin tabs under `app/views/settings/_*.html.erb` via
  `setting_check_box`, `setting_text_field` (`app/helpers/settings_helper.rb:97-110`).
  See `app/views/settings/_api.html.erb` for the API tab.

## Migrations

- File name `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_verb_noun.rb`, class `ActiveRecord::Migration[7.2]`,
  `def change` with reversible operations (`db/migrate/20250611092155_create_doorkeeper_tables.rb`,
  `..._enable_pkce.rb`). No GPL header.
- `db/schema.rb` is gitignored; it is never committed. Structure is expressed only by
  migrations, so they must be complete (indexes, null constraints, foreign keys where
  Redmine uses them; note that Redmine mostly does not use DB-level foreign keys).
- Must run on PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite: no database-specific SQL or types.

## Tests (minitest, `test/`)

- Layout: `test/unit/<model>_test.rb` (class `XxxTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase`),
  `test/functional/<controller>_test.rb` (`XxxControllerTest < Redmine::ControllerTest`,
  `test/test_helper.rb:353`), `test/integration/...` (`Redmine::IntegrationTest`,
  line 406), `test/integration/api_test/<name>_test.rb`
  (`Redmine::ApiTest::XxxTest < Redmine::ApiTest::Base`, line 437). `test/system/`
  exists but is browser-based; not needed for this slice.
- Every test file starts with the GPL header, then `require_relative '../test_helper'`
  (depth-adjusted), then the class.
- **Test names are `def test_should_do_something`** (289 files) rather than the
  `test "..." do` form (47 files). Use `def test_...`, descriptive, snake_case.
- Fixtures: `fixtures :all` is loaded globally (`test_helper.rb:59`), so
  `test/fixtures/*.yml` are always available. Known users: id 1 = admin, id 2 =
  jsmith (a regular user). `User.find(2)`, `User.find(1)` appear everywhere. A new
  table gets a fixture file `test/fixtures/<table>.yml` only if tests need seeded
  rows; otherwise create records in the test (`User.generate!`, `Token.create!`).
- Functional tests log in with `@request.session[:user_id] = 2` in `setup`
  (`test/functional/my_controller_test.rb:23`), call `get :action`, `post :action,
  :params => {...}`, and assert with `assert_response`, `assert_redirected_to`,
  `assert_select 'css', 'text'`, `assert_select_error`.
- API tests use `credentials(user_login_or_key, password)` for HTTP Basic headers
  (`test_helper.rb:428`) and `Redmine::ApiTest::Base` which enables the REST API for
  the duration of the test. Template: `test/integration/api_test/authentication_test.rb`.
- Helpers to reuse: `with_settings(:key => value) { ... }` (`test_helper.rb:97`),

# Redmine code and test conventions (as found in 6.1.2)

Canonical reference for the implementer and the reviewer. Everything here was read
from the 6.1.2 tree or the official wiki on 2026-09-07; file pointers are given so it
can be re-verified. Where Redmine has no written rule, the convention is "do what the
surrounding code does", and the pointers show what that is.

## Sources

- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: development happens on redmine.org, not GitHub. Patches must
  include tests and all existing tests must pass.
- Wiki "Coding Standards" (redmine.org/projects/redmine/wiki/Coding_Standards):
  "Make sure any new code is tested, especially in the Controllers and Models. Code
  without tests may (and probably will) be rejected on that reason alone." Prefer
  `blank?`/`present?` over `empty?`/`nil?` in views. Document methods as needed and
  explain any complex code. Otherwise follow the Rails contributing conventions.
- `.rubocop.yml` + `.rubocop_todo.yml`: enforced in CI (`.github/workflows/linters.yml`
  runs `bundle exec rubocop --parallel`). Also `bundle audit` and stylelint on CSS.
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml`: the suite runs on Ruby 3.2/3.3/3.4 against
  PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite. Anything we write must be portable across all three.
- `doc/RUNNING_TESTS`, `lib/tasks/testing.rake`.

## Ruby source files

- **Every Ruby file starts with** `# frozen_string_literal: true`, a blank line, then
  the GPL header exactly as in `app/models/token.rb:1-18`. Migrations are the
  exception: `# frozen_string_literal: true` only (see `db/migrate/20250611092227_enable_pkce.rb`).
- **Hash syntax:** Redmine overwhelmingly uses the rocket style `:key => value`
  (about 2300 occurrences in `app/` versus a handful of `key: value`). Use rockets in
  app code and tests to match neighbors. Migrations and newer files use `key: value`;
  match the file you are in.
- **Style is RuboCop-enforced** with Redmine's own exceptions: metrics cops are
  disabled (`Metrics: Enabled: false`), spacing inside braces is free
  (`Layout/SpaceInsideBlockBraces`, `SpaceInsideHashLiteralBraces` disabled), line
  length has allowances for test names. Do not fight `.rubocop_todo.yml` in files we
  touch; do not add new offenses. Run before every commit:
  `docker compose exec app bundle exec rubocop <changed files>`.
- Target Ruby 3.2 (`TargetRubyVersion: 3.2`): no syntax newer than 3.2.
- Naming: models singular CamelCase in `app/models/`, controllers plural
  `XxxController` in `app/controllers/`, tests mirror the path under `test/`.

## Models

- Inherit from `ApplicationRecord`. Look at `app/models/token.rb` for the size and
  shape of a small model.
- **Mass assignment goes through `safe_attributes`**, Redmine's own mechanism, not
  strong parameters (`app/models/user.rb:819-845`; module in
  `lib/redmine/safe_attributes.rb`). Controllers assign with
  `record.safe_attributes = params[:record]`.
- Access control is `User#allowed_to?` and `Redmine::AccessControl`
  (`lib/redmine/access_control.rb`), not custom checks.
- `User.current` is the request-scoped current user; it is set by the controller.
- Validations use ActiveRecord; error messages come from i18n keys.

## Controllers

- Inherit from `ApplicationController`. Auth filters are declarative:
  `before_action :require_login` (`app/controllers/my_controller.rb:22`),
  `before_action :require_admin` (`app/controllers/settings_controller.rb:27`),
  `require_sudo_mode :action_a, :action_b` (`my_controller.rb:28-29`) for sensitive
  actions. `accept_api_auth :index, :show` declares which actions accept API keys.
- Success flows set `flash[:notice] = l(:notice_...)` and `redirect_to`. Failure
  re-renders the form. See `my_controller.rb:50-75`.
- Routes are explicit in `config/routes.rb` (`my/*` block at line 92). Use `:as` to
  name routes so views can use `xxx_path` helpers; never hardcode URLs in views.
- API responses use `respond_to` with `format.api` and the `.api.rsb` builder views
  (`app/views/my/account.api.rsb`).

## Views (ERB)

- Plain ERB, no other templating. Every user-visible string is `l(:key)` from
  `config/locales/en.yml`. Never a literal English string in a view.
- List pages follow `app/views/auth_sources/index.html.erb`: a `div.contextual` with
  the add link, `<%= title l(:label_xxx_plural) %>`, `<table class="list">` with
  `thead`/`tbody`, rows with `id="record-<id>"`, a `td.buttons` cell using
  `delete_link` (`app/helpers/application_helper.rb:1600`) and `sprite_icon`
  (`app/helpers/icons_helper.rb:36`).
- Sidebars use `content_for :sidebar` (`app/views/my/account.html.erb:75`); page
  titles use `html_title` (line 79). `app/views/my/_sidebar.html.erb` is a partial
  (leading underscore).
- Forms use `labelled_form_for` / `form_tag` with `f.text_field` etc.; look at
  `app/views/my/password.html.erb` for a small form.
- New CSS goes in `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css` and must pass stylelint
  (`.stylelintrc`). Prefer reusing existing classes.
- JavaScript: Stimulus controllers exist (`data-controller="api-key-copy"` in
  `_sidebar.html.erb:23`), plus jQuery. Only add JS if the spec needs it.

## i18n

- Add keys only to `config/locales/en.yml`. Do not touch the other 49 locale files;
  `rake locales:update` propagates English keys to them and maintainers do that.
- Key prefixes: `label_` (nouns, page titles), `field_` (attribute names, used by
  ActiveRecord error messages via `activerecord` mapping too), `button_` (actions),
  `text_` (sentences, help text), `notice_` (flash success), `error_` (flash/validation
  failures), `setting_` (admin settings labels). Plurals are `label_xxx_plural`.
- Run `docker compose exec app bin/rails locales:check_interpolation` if a key uses
  `%{placeholders}`.

## Settings

- Declared in `config/settings.yml` with a default; accessed as `Setting.xxx` /
  `Setting.xxx?`; rendered in admin tabs under `app/views/settings/_*.html.erb` via
  `setting_check_box`, `setting_text_field` (`app/helpers/settings_helper.rb:97-110`).
  See `app/views/settings/_api.html.erb` for the API tab.

## Migrations

- File name `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_verb_noun.rb`, class `ActiveRecord::Migration[7.2]`,
  `def change` with reversible operations (`db/migrate/20250611092155_create_doorkeeper_tables.rb`,
  `..._enable_pkce.rb`). No GPL header.
- `db/schema.rb` is gitignored; it is never committed. Structure is expressed only by
  migrations, so they must be complete (indexes, null constraints, foreign keys where
  Redmine uses them; note that Redmine mostly does not use DB-level foreign keys).
- Must run on PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite: no database-specific SQL or types.

## Tests (minitest, `test/`)

- Layout: `test/unit/<model>_test.rb` (class `XxxTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase`),
  `test/functional/<controller>_test.rb` (`XxxControllerTest < Redmine::ControllerTest`,
  `test/test_helper.rb:353`), `test/integration/...` (`Redmine::IntegrationTest`,
  line 406), `test/integration/api_test/<name>_test.rb`
  (`Redmine::ApiTest::XxxTest < Redmine::ApiTest::Base`, line 437). `test/system/`
  exists but is browser-based; not needed for this slice.
- Every test file starts with the GPL header, then `require_relative '../test_helper'`
  (depth-adjusted), then the class.
- **Test names are `def test_should_do_something`** (289 files) rather than the
  `test "..." do` form (47 files). Use `def test_...`, descriptive, snake_case.
- Fixtures: `fixtures :all` is loaded globally (`test_helper.rb:59`), so
  `test/fixtures/*.yml` are always available. Known users: id 1 = admin, id 2 =
  jsmith (a regular user). `User.find(2)`, `User.find(1)` appear everywhere. A new
  table gets a fixture file `test/fixtures/<table>.yml` only if tests need seeded
  rows; otherwise create records in the test (`User.generate!`, `Token.create!`).
- Functional tests log in with `@request.session[:user_id] = 2` in `setup`
  (`test/functional/my_controller_test.rb:23`), call `get :action`, `post :action,
  :params => {...}`, and assert with `assert_response`, `assert_redirected_to`,
  `assert_select 'css', 'text'`, `assert_select_error`.
- API tests use `credentials(user_login_or_key, password)` for HTTP Basic headers
  (`test_helper.rb:428`) and `Redmine::ApiTest::Base` which enables the REST API for
  the duration of the test. Template: `test/integration/api_test/authentication_test.rb`.
- Helpers to reuse: `with_settings(:key => value) { ... }` (`test_helper.rb:97`),
  `with_current_user(user) { ... }` (line 115), `assert_difference 'Model.count'`,
  `assert_no_difference`, `assert_save`, `assert_include`.
- `setup` often resets `User.current = nil`; API tests do so in `teardown`.
- Cover both the success path and every failure path (unauthorized, forbidden,
  expired, invalid). Auth code is the area where maintainers demand it most.
- Run: `docker compose exec app bin/rails test test/unit/xxx_test.rb`, a single test
  with `-n test_name`, the touched areas together, and `bin/rails test` for the full
  suite before the MR. `bin/rails test:autoload` is part of CI too.

1 # Feature specification: Personal access tokens for the Redmine REST API 2 3 File: `ai-workflow/specs/07_09_22_31_PAT_tokens_spec.md` (feature slug `PAT_tokens`, created 2026-09-07 22:31). 4 5 Status: **draft v1, 2026-09-07, all planner/human questions resolved, awaiting critic 6 round 1**. Not yet approved by the human. 7 8 Owner: planner (`ai-workflow/roles/planner.md`). This document is the implementer's 9 contract. Anything not covered here is a question to the human, not an improvisation. 10 Decisions are referenced as `D-NNN` (`ai-workflow/decisions.md`); Redmine facts as 11 sections of `ai-workflow/architecture.md` (`arch 1.x`). Follow `ai-workflow/conventions.md`. 12 13 Rails and Redmine mechanisms are explained where they first matter, in *italics*, for 14 the human's benefit; the implementer can skip those. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## 1. Goal and non-goals 19 20 **Goal.** Give every Redmine user self-service personal access tokens (PATs) for the 21 REST API: several named tokens per user, each with a mandatory expiry, stored hashed, 22 shown in plaintext exactly once, with last-used tracking and one-click revocation from 23 "My account". An admin can cap the maximum lifetime. Legacy API keys keep working 24 unchanged, and a PAT is accepted on every transport the legacy key is accepted on. 25 Following the core maintainer's direction in #43881, a PAT is not a new kind of secret: 26 it is a Doorkeeper OAuth access token that has no application and is issued directly 27 by its owner (D-010). 28 29 **Non-goals (deferred, with reasons).** 30 31 - Scopes per token (pillar 2): the data path exists (`scopes` column, `User#oauth_scope`), 32 the UI does not. Deferred by D-004; a core PAT has blank scopes = full access. 33 - Admin overview of all tokens (ticket phase one mentions it): deferred; first 34 candidate add-on after the core is reviewed (D-005). 35 - Per-role permission to create tokens (Dennis Buehring's request), a switch to 36 disable legacy keys, audit logging (pillar 4), endpoint control (pillar 5), CORS 37 (pillar 6): out of the core slice. 38 - Rate limiting (pillar 3): forbidden (D-002). 39 - A JSON/XML API to manage tokens: self-service is UI only in this slice. 40 - Emailing the user on token creation/revocation: not in this slice. 41 42 ## 2. Design decision summary 43 44 | Topic | Decision | Entry | 45 |---|---|---| 46 | Model | PAT = `Doorkeeper::AccessToken` row with `application_id NULL`, via subclass `PersonalAccessToken` | D-010 | 47 | Columns | `name`, `last_used_at`, `token_suffix` added to `oauth_access_tokens` | D-009, D-010 | 48 | Format | `rmpat_` + Doorkeeper's 43-char random part; SHA-256 at rest (Doorkeeper `hash_token_secrets`) | D-011 | 49 | Expiry | Mandatory, lifetime picker 7/30/60/90/180/365 days → `expires_in` seconds | D-006 | 50 | Admin cap | `Setting.personal_access_token_max_lifetime` (days, 0 = no cap), API tab | D-008 | 51 | Transports | Bearer, `access_token`/`bearer_token` params, `X-Redmine-API-Key`, `?key=`, Basic username | D-012 | 52 | Log filtering | `key` and `bearer_token` added to `filter_parameters` now | D-012, D-016 | 53 | Full access | Blank scopes on an app-less token → `oauth_scope` is not set | D-010 | 54 | Last used | Direct column write, 1-minute throttle | D-013 | 55 | Revocation | `revoked_at` set, row kept; expired tokens listed until revoked | D-014 | 56 | UI | Page `my/api_tokens`, new controller, sidebar untouched, link in My account contextual bar | D-005 | 57 | Show once | Redirect after create, plaintext one hop in the flash, `no_store`, notice on refresh | D-007 | 58 | User deletion | Delete the user's OAuth tokens and grants before destroy; separate first commit; README item | D-015 | 59 60 ## 3. Data model 61 62 ### 3.1 Migration 63 64 File: `db/migrate/20260907120000_add_personal_access_token_columns_to_oauth_access_tokens.rb` 65 (timestamp: any value later than `20250611092227`, use the real creation time). 66 Class `ActiveRecord::Migration[7.2]`, `def change`, `key: value` hash style (matches 67 neighbouring migrations, `arch 1.7`), no GPL header, `# frozen_string_literal: true`. 68 69 ```ruby 70 add_column :oauth_access_tokens, :name, :string, limit: 255 71 add_column :oauth_access_tokens, :last_used_at, :datetime 72 add_column :oauth_access_tokens, :token_suffix, :string, limit: 4 73 ``` 74 75 All nullable: OAuth-flow tokens have none of these. No new index: lookups are by 76 `token` (unique index exists) and by `resource_owner_id` (index exists, 77 `20250611092155_create_doorkeeper_tables.rb:54`). Must run on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite; 78 `add_column` with these types does. 79 80 *A migration is a versioned Ruby script that changes the database schema; Rails 81 records which ones ran in `schema_migrations`. `db/schema.rb` is gitignored in Redmine, 82 so the migration is the only description of the columns.* 83 84 ### 3.2 Model `app/models/personal_access_token.rb` 85 86 ```ruby 87 class PersonalAccessToken < Doorkeeper::AccessToken 88 include Redmine::SafeAttributes 89 90 TOKEN_PREFIX = 'rmpat_' 91 LIFETIMES = [7, 30, 60, 90, 180, 365] # days, same list as password_max_age 92 93 belongs_to :user, :foreign_key => 'resource_owner_id' 94 95 scope :personal, lambda {where(:application_id => nil)} 96 scope :not_revoked, lambda {where(:revoked_at => nil)} 97 98 attr_accessor :lifetime_days # virtual attribute fed by the form 99 100 safe_attributes 'name', 'lifetime_days' 101 102 validates :name, :presence => true, :length => {:maximum => 255} 103 validates :name, :uniqueness => {:scope => :resource_owner_id, 104 :conditions => -> { personal.not_revoked }, 105 :case_sensitive => false} 106 validates :application_id, :absence => true 107 validates :lifetime_days, :inclusion => {:in => ->(t) { PersonalAccessToken.allowed_lifetimes }}, 108 :on => :create 109 validates :expires_in, :presence => true 110 111 before_validation :set_expiry, :on => :create 112 # use_refresh_token is false by default (attr_writer in the mixin); never set it. 113 ``` 114 115 Behaviour, all to be implemented in this class (Doorkeeper base class untouched): 116 117 - `set_expiry`: `self.expires_in = lifetime_days.to_i.days.to_i` when `lifetime_days` 118 is present. `scopes` stays blank (`''`): blank = full access (D-010). 119 - `self.allowed_lifetimes`: `LIFETIMES` filtered by 120 `Setting.personal_access_token_max_lifetime.to_i` when that is > 0 (keep values 121 `<= cap`). If the cap is smaller than 7, the list is empty and creation is 122 impossible; the form shows `text_personal_access_token_no_lifetime_available`. 123 - `token_generator` (instance method, overrides `access_token_mixin.rb:503`): returns 124 an object whose `generate(opts)` yields 125 `TOKEN_PREFIX + Doorkeeper::OAuth::Helpers::UniqueToken.generate(opts)`. The base 126 `generate_token` (l.472-478) then stores `SHA256(plaintext)` and keeps the plaintext 127 in `@raw_token` / `#plaintext_token`. 128 - `generate_token` override: `super`, then `self.token_suffix = plaintext_token.last(4)`. 129 - `expired?`, `revoked?`, `accessible?`, `revoke`, `expires_at` come from Doorkeeper 130 (`arch 1.3.1`). Add `def active?; accessible?; end` only if a view needs the name. 131 - `self.track_use(access_token)`: class method taking the `Doorkeeper::AccessToken` 132 found during authentication (Doorkeeper instantiates its base class, not ours). 133 Returns unless `access_token.application_id.nil?`. Skips the write when 134 `last_used_at` is present and `>= 1.minute.ago`; otherwise 135 `where(:id => access_token.id).update_all(:last_used_at => Time.now)`. Mirrors 136 `User#update_last_login_on!` (`user.rb:328-331`, D-013). 137 - `self.full_access?(access_token)`: `access_token.application_id.nil? && 138 access_token.scopes.all.empty?`. Used by `find_current_user`. 139 140 *`Doorkeeper::AccessToken` is an ActiveRecord model owned by the gem. Subclassing it 141 without a `type` column means both classes read and write the same table; our class 142 adds validations and helpers, and `scope :personal` narrows queries to our rows.* 143 *`safe_attributes` is Redmine's whitelist for mass assignment: the controller writes 144 `token.safe_attributes = params[:personal_access_token]` and only listed attributes 145 are copied (`lib/redmine/safe_attributes.rb`).* 146 *`attr_accessor :lifetime_days` declares a plain Ruby attribute that is not a column; 147 the form posts it, the callback turns it into `expires_in`.* 148 149 ### 3.3 `User` additions (`app/models/user.rb`) 150 151 - `has_many :personal_access_tokens, lambda {where(:application_id => nil)}, 152 :foreign_key => 'resource_owner_id', :dependent => nil` next to `:api_token` (l.102). 153 No `dependent` option: deletion is handled below. 154 - `remove_references_before_destroy` (l.971-993): add 155 `Doorkeeper::AccessToken.where(:resource_owner_id => id).delete_all` and 156 `Doorkeeper::AccessGrant.where(:resource_owner_id => id).delete_all` next to the 157 `Token` line (l.993). This is the D-015 fix, shipped as its own commit. 158 159 ## 4. Authentication flow 160 161 ### 4.1 Where a PAT can be presented 162 163 Configured in `config/initializers/30-redmine.rb` inside `Doorkeeper.configure` 164 (after `grant_flows`): 165 166 ```ruby 167 access_token_methods :from_bearer_authorization, 168 :from_access_token_param, 169 :from_bearer_param, 170 lambda {|request| request.headers['X-Redmine-API-Key'].presence}, 171 lambda {|request| request.params[:key].presence}, 172 :from_basic_authorization 173 ``` 174 175 `Doorkeeper::OAuth::Token.from_request` accepts symbols or callables and stops at the 176 first non-blank value (`oauth/token.rb:7-13`); `from_basic_authorization` returns the 177 Basic username (l.38-42). Order matters only for which value wins when several are 178 present; keep Redmine's legacy transports after the standard OAuth ones. 179 180 Side effect to accept: for a plain username/password Basic request, Doorkeeper now 181 does one extra `find_by(token: SHA256(username))` query that returns nil before the 182 Basic branch runs. Negligible. 183 184 ### 4.2 `find_current_user` (`app/controllers/application_controller.rb:130-158`) 185 186 Replace the API branch with: 187 188 ```ruby 189 if user.nil? && Setting.rest_api_enabled? && accept_api_auth? 190 if (key = api_key_from_request) && (user = User.find_by_api_key(key)) 191 # Legacy API key (unchanged behaviour) 192 elsif (access_token = Doorkeeper.authenticate(request)) 193 # OAuth access token or personal access token 194 if access_token.accessible? 195 user = User.active.find_by_id(access_token.resource_owner_id) 196 if user 197 user.oauth_scope = access_token.scopes.all.map(&:to_sym) unless PersonalAccessToken.full_access?(access_token) 198 PersonalAccessToken.track_use(access_token) 199 end 200 else 201 doorkeeper_render_error 202 end 203 elsif /\ABasic /i.match?(request.authorization.to_s) 204 # unchanged 205 ``` 206 207 Rules this encodes: 208 209 - **Legacy first.** A valid legacy key wins as today. An invalid value in 210 `X-Redmine-API-Key`/`?key=` no longer short-circuits: it falls to Doorkeeper, then 211 to Basic, then to the usual 401. A 40-hex legacy key can never match a PAT (hash 212 lookup) and a PAT can never match a legacy key (`Token.find_token` regex), so there 213 is no ambiguity (`arch 1.3.1`). 214 - **Locked/registered users.** `User.active.find_by_id` returns nil → no user → 401. 215 The `if user` guard also fixes a latent `NoMethodError` on `nil.oauth_scope=` for 216 locked OAuth users (test it). 217 - **Full access vs scoped.** App-less token with blank scopes → `oauth_scope` is not 218 set, so `User#admin?` and `allowed_to?` behave exactly as with a legacy key 219 (`arch 1.3.1`, D-010). A token with scopes (OAuth flow today, scoped PATs later) → 220 unchanged behaviour. 221 - **Expired or revoked** → `doorkeeper_render_error`: 401 with 222 `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="Redmine", error="invalid_token", ...`. Unknown token 223 → falls through → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Redmine API"` from 224 `require_login`. Both are 401; the header differs. Documented as a known 225 difference, not changed. 226 - **REST API disabled** → this whole branch is skipped; 403 as today 227 (`disabled_rest_api_test.rb`). 228 - `must_change_password?` and 2FA are not checked for PATs, same as legacy keys 229 (`arch 1.10`). `X-Redmine-Switch-User` still applies afterwards (l.160-168). 230 231 *`find_current_user` runs before every action (`before_action :user_setup`) and sets 232 `User.current`; authorisation happens later in `authorize`. API requests never use the 233 session (`arch 1.1`).* 234 235 ### 4.3 Log filtering (`config/application.rb:68`) 236 237 ```ruby 238 config.filter_parameters += [:password, /\Akey\z/, /\Abearer_token\z/] 239 ``` 240 241 Anchored, like Doorkeeper's own filter (`doorkeeper/engine.rb:9`), so unrelated 242 parameters containing "key" are not masked. Doorkeeper already filters 243 `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `client_secret`, `code`. Headers are not logged by 244 Rails. (D-012, D-016) 245 246 ## 5. # Feature specification: Personal access tokens for the Redmine REST API File: `ai-workflow/specs/07_09_22_31_PAT_tokens_spec.md` (feature slug `PAT_tokens`, created 2026-09-07 22:31). Status: **draft v1, 2026-09-07, all planner/human questions resolved, awaiting critic round 1**. Not yet approved by the human. Owner: planner (`ai-workflow/roles/planner.md`). This document is the implementer's contract. Anything not covered here is a question to the human, not an improvisation. Decisions are referenced as `D-NNN` (`ai-workflow/decisions.md`); Redmine facts as sections of `ai-workflow/architecture.md` (`arch 1.x`). Follow `ai-workflow/conventions.md`. Rails and Redmine mechanisms are explained where they first matter, in *italics*, for the human's benefit; the implementer can skip those. --- ## 1. Goal and non-goals **Goal.** Give every Redmine user self-service personal access tokens (PATs) for the REST API: several named tokens per user, each with a mandatory expiry, stored hashed, shown in plaintext exactly once, with last-used tracking and one-click revocation from "My account". An admin can cap the maximum lifetime. Legacy API keys keep working unchanged, and a PAT is accepted on every transport the legacy key is accepted on. Following the core maintainer's direction in #43881, a PAT is not a new kind of secret: it is a Doorkeeper OAuth access token that has no application and is issued directly by its owner (D-010). **Non-goals (deferred, with reasons).** - Scopes per token (pillar 2): the data path exists (`scopes` column, `User#oauth_scope`), the UI does not. Deferred by D-004; a core PAT has blank scopes = full access. - Admin overview of all tokens (ticket phase one mentions it): deferred; first candidate add-on after the core is reviewed (D-005). - Per-role permission to create tokens (Dennis Buehring's request), a switch to disable legacy keys, audit logging (pillar 4), endpoint control (pillar 5), CORS (pillar 6): out of the core slice. - Rate limiting (pillar 3): forbidden (D-002). - A JSON/XML API to manage tokens: self-service is UI only in this slice. - Emailing the user on token creation/revocation: not in this slice. ## 2. Design decision summary | Topic | Decision | Entry | |---|---|---| | Model | PAT = `Doorkeeper::AccessToken` row with `application_id NULL`, via subclass `PersonalAccessToken` | D-010 | | Columns | `name`, `last_used_at`, `token_suffix` added to `oauth_access_tokens` | D-009, D-010 | | Format | `rmpat_` + Doorkeeper's 43-char random part; SHA-256 at rest (Doorkeeper `hash_token_secrets`) | D-011 | | Expiry | Mandatory, lifetime picker 7/30/60/90/180/365 days → `expires_in` seconds | D-006 | | Admin cap | `Setting.personal_access_token_max_lifetime` (days, 0 = no cap), API tab | D-008 | | Transports | Bearer, `access_token`/`bearer_token` params, `X-Redmine-API-Key`, `?key=`, Basic username | D-012 | | Log filtering | `key` and `bearer_token` added to `filter_parameters` now | D-012, D-016 | | Full access | Blank scopes on an app-less token → `oauth_scope` is not set | D-010 | | Last used | Direct column write, 1-minute throttle | D-013 | | Revocation | `revoked_at` set, row kept; expired tokens listed until revoked | D-014 | | UI | Page `my/api_tokens`, new controller, sidebar untouched, link in My account contextual bar | D-005 | | Show once | Redirect after create, plaintext one hop in the flash, `no_store`, notice on refresh | D-007 | | User deletion | Delete the user's OAuth tokens and grants before destroy; separate first commit; README item | D-015 | ## 3. Data model ### 3.1 Migration File: `db/migrate/20260907120000_add_personal_access_token_columns_to_oauth_access_tokens.rb` (timestamp: any value later than `20250611092227`, use the real creation time). Class `ActiveRecord::Migration[7.2]`, `def change`, `key: value` hash style (matches neighbouring migrations, `arch 1.7`), no GPL header, `# frozen_string_literal: true`. ```ruby add_column :oauth_access_tokens, :name, :string, limit: 255 add_column :oauth_access_tokens, :last_used_at, :datetime add_column :oauth_access_tokens, :token_suffix, :string, limit: 4 ``` All nullable: OAuth-flow tokens have none of these. No new index: lookups are by `token` (unique index exists) and by `resource_owner_id` (index exists, `20250611092155_create_doorkeeper_tables.rb:54`). Must run on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite; `add_column` with these types does. *A migration is a versioned Ruby script that changes the database schema; Rails records which ones ran in `schema_migrations`. `db/schema.rb` is gitignored in Redmine, so the migration is the only description of the columns.* ### 3.2 Model `app/models/personal_access_token.rb` ```ruby class PersonalAccessToken < Doorkeeper::AccessToken include Redmine::SafeAttributes TOKEN_PREFIX = 'rmpat_' LIFETIMES = [7, 30, 60, 90, 180, 365] # days, same list as password_max_age belongs_to :user, :foreign_key => 'resource_owner_id' scope :personal, lambda {where(:application_id => nil)} scope :not_revoked, lambda {where(:revoked_at => nil)} attr_accessor :lifetime_days # virtual attribute fed by the form safe_attributes 'name', 'lifetime_days' validates :name, :presence => true, :length => {:maximum => 255} validates :name, :uniqueness => {:scope => :resource_owner_id, :conditions => -> { personal.not_revoked }, :case_sensitive => false} validates :application_id, :absence => true validates :lifetime_days, :inclusion => {:in => ->(t) { PersonalAccessToken.allowed_lifetimes }}, :on => :create validates :expires_in, :presence => true before_validation :set_expiry, :on => :create # use_refresh_token is false by default (attr_writer in the mixin); never set it. ``` Behaviour, all to be implemented in this class (Doorkeeper base class untouched): - `set_expiry`: `self.expires_in = lifetime_days.to_i.days.to_i` when `lifetime_days` is present. `scopes` stays blank (`''`): blank = full access (D-010). - `self.allowed_lifetimes`: `LIFETIMES` filtered by `Setting.personal_access_token_max_lifetime.to_i` when that is > 0 (keep values `<= cap`). If the cap is smaller than 7, the list is empty and creation is impossible; the form shows `text_personal_access_token_no_lifetime_available`. - `token_generator` (instance method, overrides `access_token_mixin.rb:503`): returns an object whose `generate(opts)` yields `TOKEN_PREFIX + Doorkeeper::OAuth::Helpers::UniqueToken.generate(opts)`. The base `generate_token` (l.472-478) then stores `SHA256(plaintext)` and keeps the plaintext in `@raw_token` / `#plaintext_token`. - `generate_token` override: `super`, then `self.token_suffix = plaintext_token.last(4)`. - `expired?`, `revoked?`, `accessible?`, `revoke`, `expires_at` come from Doorkeeper (`arch 1.3.1`). Add `def active?; accessible?; end` only if a view needs the name. - `self.track_use(access_token)`: class method taking the `Doorkeeper::AccessToken` found during authentication (Doorkeeper instantiates its base class, not ours). Returns unless `access_token.application_id.nil?`. Skips the write when `last_used_at` is present and `>= 1.minute.ago`; otherwise `where(:id => access_token.id).update_all(:last_used_at => Time.now)`. Mirrors `User#update_last_login_on!` (`user.rb:328-331`, D-013). - `self.full_access?(access_token)`: `access_token.application_id.nil? && access_token.scopes.all.empty?`. Used by `find_current_user`. *`Doorkeeper::AccessToken` is an ActiveRecord model owned by the gem. Subclassing it without a `type` column means both classes read and write the same table; our class adds validations and helpers, and `scope :personal` narrows queries to our rows.* *`safe_attributes` is Redmine's whitelist for mass assignment: the controller writes `token.safe_attributes = params[:personal_access_token]` and only listed attributes are copied (`lib/redmine/safe_attributes.rb`).* *`attr_accessor :lifetime_days` declares a plain Ruby attribute that is not a column; the form posts it, the callback turns it into `expires_in`.* ### 3.3 `User` additions (`app/models/user.rb`) - `has_many :personal_access_tokens, lambda {where(:application_id => nil)}, :foreign_key => 'resource_owner_id', :dependent => nil` next to `:api_token` (l.102). No `dependent` option: deletion is handled below. - `remove_references_before_destroy` (l.971-993): add `Doorkeeper::AccessToken.where(:resource_owner_id => id).delete_all` and `Doorkeeper::AccessGrant.where(:resource_owner_id => id).delete_all` next to the `Token` line (l.993). This is the D-015 fix, shipped as its own commit. ## 4. Authentication flow ### 4.1 Where a PAT can be presented Configured in `config/initializers/30-redmine.rb` inside `Doorkeeper.configure` (after `grant_flows`): ```ruby access_token_methods :from_bearer_authorization, :from_access_token_param, :from_bearer_param, lambda {|request| request.headers['X-Redmine-API-Key'].presence}, lambda {|request| request.params[:key].presence}, :from_basic_authorization ``` `Doorkeeper::OAuth::Token.from_request` accepts symbols or callables and stops at the first non-blank value (`oauth/token.rb:7-13`); `from_basic_authorization` returns the Basic username (l.38-42). Order matters only for which value wins when several are present; keep Redmine's legacy transports after the standard OAuth ones. Side effect to accept: for a plain username/password Basic request, Doorkeeper now does one extra `find_by(token: SHA256(username))` query that returns nil before the Basic branch runs. Negligible. ### 4.2 `find_current_user` (`app/controllers/application_controller.rb:130-158`) Replace the API branch with: ```ruby if user.nil? && Setting.rest_api_enabled? && accept_api_auth? if (key = api_key_from_request) && (user = User.find_by_api_key(key)) # Legacy API key (unchanged behaviour) elsif (access_token = Doorkeeper.authenticate(request)) # OAuth access token or personal access token if access_token.accessible? user = User.active.find_by_id(access_token.resource_owner_id) if user user.oauth_scope = access_token.scopes.all.map(&:to_sym) unless PersonalAccessToken.full_access?(access_token) PersonalAccessToken.track_use(access_token) end else doorkeeper_render_error end elsif /\ABasic /i.match?(request.authorization.to_s) # unchanged ``` Rules this encodes: - **Legacy first.** A valid legacy key wins as today. An invalid value in `X-Redmine-API-Key`/`?key=` no longer short-circuits: it falls to Doorkeeper, then to Basic, then to the usual 401. A 40-hex legacy key can never match a PAT (hash lookup) and a PAT can never match a legacy key (`Token.find_token` regex), so there is no ambiguity (`arch 1.3.1`). - **Locked/registered users.** `User.active.find_by_id` returns nil → no user → 401. The `if user` guard also fixes a latent `NoMethodError` on `nil.oauth_scope=` for locked OAuth users (test it). - **Full access vs scoped.** App-less token with blank scopes → `oauth_scope` is not set, so `User#admin?` and `allowed_to?` behave exactly as with a legacy key (`arch 1.3.1`, D-010). A token with scopes (OAuth flow today, scoped PATs later) → unchanged behaviour. - **Expired or revoked** → `doorkeeper_render_error`: 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="Redmine", error="invalid_token", ...`. Unknown token → falls through → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Redmine API"` from `require_login`. Both are 401; the header differs. Documented as a known difference, not changed. - **REST API disabled** → this whole branch is skipped; 403 as today (`disabled_rest_api_test.rb`). - `must_change_password?` and 2FA are not checked for PATs, same as legacy keys (`arch 1.10`). `X-Redmine-Switch-User` still applies afterwards (l.160-168). *`find_current_user` runs before every action (`before_action :user_setup`) and sets `User.current`; authorisation happens later in `authorize`. API requests never use the session (`arch 1.1`).* ### 4.3 Log filtering (`config/application.rb:68`) ```ruby config.filter_parameters += [:password, /\Akey\z/, /\Abearer_token\z/] ``` Anchored, like Doorkeeper's own filter (`doorkeeper/engine.rb:9`), so unrelated parameters containing "key" are not masked. Doorkeeper already filters `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `client_secret`, `code`. Headers are not logged by Rails. (D-012, D-016) ## 5. ## 6. Settings

`config/settings.yml`, after `rest_api_enabled`/`jsonp_enabled` (l.333-338):

```yaml
personal_access_token_max_lifetime:
  format: int
  default: 0
  security_notifications: 1
```

`app/views/settings/_api.html.erb`, third `
`:

```erb

<%= setting_select :personal_access_token_max_lifetime,
       [[l(:label_disabled), 0]] + PersonalAccessToken::LIFETIMES.collect {|days| [l('datetime.distance_in_words.x_days', :count => days), days.to_s]} %>

```

Semantics (D-008): 0 = no cap; otherwise the picker offers only lifetimes `<= cap`
and the model rejects anything else. Applies at creation; existing tokens are not
shortened. `security_notifications: 1` emails admins on change, like
`password_max_age`.

## 7. Optional pillars included

None. Scopes are deliberately left as a UI-only follow-up: the column, the
`oauth_scope` enforcement and the "blank = full access" rule are all in place.

## 8. Testing strategy

All tests: GPL header, `require_relative`, `def test_...` names, rocket hashes,
`fixtures :all` is global. Run in Docker: `docker compose exec app bin/rails test `.
Create tokens with `PersonalAccessToken.create!(:user => User.find(2), :name => 'x', :lifetime_days => 30)`;
add `PersonalAccessToken.generate!(attributes={})` to `test/object_helpers.rb`
(pattern of `User.generate!`, l.4-15) with defaults `user: User.find(2)`,
`name: "token#{n}"`, `lifetime_days: 30`, returning the saved record (its
`plaintext_token` is readable in the test). No fixture file: hashed values in YAML
would obscure the tests.

1	# Architecture
2	
3	Living document. Two halves: what we have learned about Redmine that matters for this
4	task, and what we have built, how, and why. Keep it current; a reader who only has this

7	## 1. Findings about Redmine 6.1.2
8	
9	Status: **investigated 2026-09-07** by the planner against the checkout at the workspace
10	root (branch `feature/personal-access-tokens`, from tag 6.1.2, commit `1b5585ca9`).
11	All paths are relative to the workspace root; line numbers are from that commit.
12	Stack: Rails 7.2.3, Doorkeeper 5.8.2, bcrypt 3.1.22 (`Gemfile.lock`).
13	
14	### 1.1 API authentication dispatch
15	
16	Everything happens in `app/controllers/application_controller.rb`:
17	
18	- `user_setup` (l.102) is a `before_action` that sets `User.current = find_current_user`.
19	- `api_request?` (l.723) is simply `%w(xml json).include? params[:format]`. There is no
20	  Accept-header sniffing; the URL extension decides.
21	- `find_current_user` (l.112-173):
22	  - Session, autologin cookie and Atom key are tried only when **not** `api_request?`
23	    (l.114-129). API requests never use the session (`test_api_request_should_not_use_user_session`).
24	  - The API branch (l.130) is gated by `Setting.rest_api_enabled? && accept_api_auth?`,
25	    then tries, in this order:
26	    1. `api_key_from_request` (l.728): `params[:key]` first, then header
27	       `X-Redmine-API-Key`. Resolved with `User.find_by_api_key(key)` (l.133).
28	    2. `Doorkeeper.authenticate(request)` (l.134): OAuth bearer token. If
29	       `access_token.accessible?` the user is loaded with `User.active.find_by_id` and
30	       `user.oauth_scope = access_token.scopes.all.map(&:to_sym)` is set; otherwise
31	       `doorkeeper_render_error`.
32	    3. HTTP Basic (l.142): only if `request.authorization` starts with `Basic`.
33	       `User.try_to_login(username, password)` first; if that user has 2FA active the
34	       request is rejected with 401 "HTTP Basic authentication is not allowed. Use API
35	       key instead" (l.147-150). Then `user ||= User.find_by_api_key(username)`, i.e. the
36	       API key can be sent as the Basic username with any password (l.152).
37	       `must_change_password?` is checked with a 403 **only inside this Basic branch**
38	       (l.154-157); the header/param API-key path does not check it.
39	  - Admin impersonation: header `X-Redmine-Switch-User` (l.160-168), admins only, 412 on
40	    invalid/locked target.
41	  - `user.remote_ip = request.remote_ip` is stored ephemerally (l.171).
42	- `accept_api_auth` (class method, l.646) stores a per-controller list of actions in
43	  `accept_api_auth_actions`; `accept_api_auth?` (l.654) checks the current action. An API
44	  key is therefore only honoured on actions that opt in (e.g. `MyController` opts in
45	  `:account` only, `app/controllers/my_controller.rb:26`).
46	- `require_login` (l.273) for `format.api` returns `401` with
47	  `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Redmine API"` when the API is enabled and the action
48	  accepts API auth, otherwise `403` (l.292-298). This is what "disabled REST API" looks
49	  like from outside (`test/integration/api_test/disabled_rest_api_test.rb`).
50	- CSRF is skipped for `api_request?` (`verify_authenticity_token`, l.43).
51	- `require_admin_or_api_request` (l.606) and `render_api_ok/head/errors` (l.761-780) are
52	  the helpers API controllers use.
53	- `Setting.rest_api_enabled?` is a plain setting (`config/settings.yml:333`, default 0,
54	  `security_notifications: 1`), toggled on the admin "API" tab
55	  (`app/views/settings/_api.html.erb`). It also gates the OAuth admin menu
56	  (`lib/redmine/preparation.rb:283-284`), the "Authorized applications" link and the
57	  API-key block in My account (`app/views/my/account.html.erb:4`, `_sidebar.html.erb:21`).
58	
59	There is no `EnabledModule` involvement in API auth; modules only matter in
60	`Project#allows_to?` inside `User#allowed_to?`.
61	
62	### 1.2 Legacy API key: `User#api_key`, `Token`, the `tokens` table
63	
64	- `app/models/token.rb`: one generic table for every kind of secret. Actions are
65	  registered with `add_action name, max_instances:, validity_time:` (l.39-45):
66	  `api` (max 1, never expires), `autologin` (10), `feeds` (1), `recovery`, `register`,
67	  `session` (10), `twofa_backup_code` (10). `add_action` accepts only those two options
68	  (`assert_valid_keys`, l.33); there is no per-row expiry, name, or last-used concept.
69	- `before_create :delete_previous_tokens, :generate_new_token` (l.24): with
70	  `max_instances: 1` for `api`, creating a second API token silently deletes the first
71	  (l.135-146). **Multiple named API tokens per user cannot be expressed with `Token`
72	  without changing its contract.**
73	- `Token.generate_token_value` = `Redmine::Utils.random_hex(20)` (l.128-130 →
74	  `lib/redmine/utils.rb:48`, `SecureRandom.hex(20)`), i.e. a 40-char lowercase hex string.
75	- `Token.find_token(action, key, validity_days=nil)` (l.113-126): rejects keys that do
76	  not match `/\A[a-z0-9]+\z/i`, does `Token.find_by(action:, value:)` on the **plaintext**
77	  value, then `secure_compare`, requires `token.user`. `find_user` / `find_active_user`
78	  (l.96-109) wrap it; `find_active_user` additionally requires `user.active?`
79	  (`status == 1`; locked/registered users are refused).
80	- **Token values are stored in plaintext.** Nothing hashes them; the unique index is on
81	  the raw value.
82	- `User#api_key` (`app/models/user.rb:443-448`) lazily creates the `api` token and
83	  returns its value; `has_one :api_token` (l.102) is the association.
84	  `User.find_by_api_key(key)` (l.553) = `Token.find_active_user('api', key)`.
85	- The `api` token is exposed via `app/views/users/show.api.rsb:14` (to admins, and to the
86	  user themself unless authorised via OAuth) and `app/views/my/account.api.rsb:10`.
87	- `User#destroy_tokens` (l.962-967) deletes `recovery`, `autologin`, `session` tokens on
88	  password change / deactivation / 2FA activation, but **not** `api`.
89	  `remove_references_before_destroy` (l.993) deletes all tokens on user destroy.
90	- Schema of `tokens` (no `db/schema.rb`: it is gitignored, `.gitignore:20`, and
91	  `db/` contains only `migrate/`):
92	  - `db/migrate/001_setup.rb:191-196`: `user_id integer not null default 0`,
93	    `action string(30)`, `value string(40)`, `created_on datetime`.
94	  - `20091017213444_add_missing_indexes_to_tokens.rb`: index on `user_id`.
95	  - `20130201184705_add_unique_index_on_tokens_value.rb`: unique index `tokens_value`.
96	  - `20151024082034_add_tokens_updated_on.rb`: `updated_on timestamp`.
97	  - Consequences: `value` is limited to 40 chars (a SHA-256 hex digest is 64), and
98	    `action` to 30. Reusing `tokens` for hashed PATs would require altering the table.
99	- Fixtures: `test/fixtures/tokens.yml` has only a `register` and a `recovery` token; no
100	  `api` token fixture exists. Tests create them with
101	  `Token.create!(:user => user, :action => 'api')`.
102	- Existing tests: `test/unit/token_test.rb` (find_token/find_active_user, expiry,
103	  max_instances), `test/unit/user_test.rb:857` (`test_api_key_should_not_be_generated_twice`),
104	  `test/functional/my_controller_test.rb:811-834` (show/reset API key),

107	### 1.3 OAuth provider (Doorkeeper, since 6.1.0)
108	
109	- Config: `config/initializers/30-redmine.rb:23-81` (the `doorkeeper.rb` initializer is
110	  an empty placeholder). Key points:
111	  - `grant_flows ['authorization_code']` only; `use_refresh_token`; PKCE enabled by
112	    migration `20250611092227_enable_pkce.rb`.
113	  - `hash_token_secrets` (Doorkeeper default strategy = SHA-256 hex of the token) and
114	    `hash_application_secrets using: '::Doorkeeper::SecretStoring::BCrypt'`. So

116	  - `access_token_expires_in` is left at the Doorkeeper default (2 hours, commented out

118	  - `default_scopes(*Redmine::AccessControl.public_permissions.map(&:name))` and

127	  - Routes: `config/routes.rb:21-22` `use_doorkeeper do controllers :applications =>
128	    'oauth2_applications' end`.
129	- Bearer token resolution for API requests is the single call
130	  `Doorkeeper.authenticate(request)` in `find_current_user` (l.134). Doorkeeper's
131	  default `access_token_methods` are `from_bearer_authorization`,
132	  `from_access_token_param`, `from_bearer_param` (Authorization: Bearer, `access_token=`,
133	  `bearer_token=`). Not verified locally (gem is not vendored in the checkout); this
134	  matches Bogdan Egikov's statement in the ticket. `X-Redmine-API-Key`, `?key=` and

136	- Scope enforcement lives in the `User` model, not the controller:
137	  - `attr_writer :oauth_scope` (`user.rb:115`); `authorized_by_oauth?` = `!@oauth_scope.nil?`
138	    (l.746).

140	  - `allowed_to?` (l.759-795) passes `@oauth_scope` into `Role#allowed_to?(action, scope)`
141	    (`app/models/role.rb:204-210`), and `Role#allowed_permissions(scope)` (l.304-311)
142	    intersects the role's permissions (plus public permissions) with the scope array.
143	    So a scope is a **filter (logical AND) over the user's real permissions**; it can
144	    never grant more than the user has. Blank scope (`nil`) = unrestricted.
145	  - This is the "reuse `User#oauth_scope`" hook Bogdan's patch relies on: set
146	    `user.oauth_scope = [...]` on a PAT-authenticated user and the existing checks apply.
147	  - Unit tests: `test/unit/user_test.rb:1401-1460` (`test_should_recognize_authorized_by_oauth`,
148	    `test_admin_should_be_limited_by_oauth_scope`, `test_oauth_scope_should_limit_*`).
149	- Tables (`db/migrate/20250611092155_create_doorkeeper_tables.rb`,
150	  `ActiveRecord::Migration[7.2]`):
151	  - `oauth_applications`: `name`, `uid` (unique), `secret`, `redirect_uri text not null`,

174	What this says about "extend OAuth" vs "standalone PAT":
175	
176	- What already exists in OAuth and would be reused by extending it: hashed token storage,
177	  `expires_in`/`revoked_at`, scopes tied to real permissions, `accessible?` semantics,
178	  admin UI for applications.
179	- What is missing for the PAT use case: (a) the only grant flow is `authorization_code`
180	  with admin-registered applications, so a user cannot self-issue a token from My
181	  account; (b) `oauth_access_tokens` has no name/last-used columns and `application_id`
182	  would have to be nil or point at a synthetic "personal" application; (c) expiry is a
183	  global config value, not per token; (d) Doorkeeper only reads `Bearer`/`access_token`,

185	  custom `access_token_methods` or a pre-resolution step in `find_current_user` anyway;
186	  (e) Doorkeeper's model classes are gem-owned; adding columns and custom lookups means
187	  monkey-patching `Doorkeeper::AccessToken`, which core reviewers dislike as much as a
188	  new model. A standalone model can still borrow the `oauth_scope` mechanism (1 line in

191	### 1.3.1 Verified: application-less Doorkeeper access tokens (probe, 2026-09-07)
192	
193	Planner probe run in the container (`bin/rails runner` + `curl`), rows deleted afterwards.
194	Gem source read at `doorkeeper-5.8.2` (installed on the host via `bundle install`).
195	
196	- `Doorkeeper::AccessToken.new(resource_owner_id:, application_id: nil, expires_in:,
197	  scopes:, use_refresh_token: false)` is **valid and saves**. `belongs_to :application`
198	  is `optional: true` (`lib/doorkeeper/orm/active_record/mixins/access_token.rb:13-15`);
199	  the only model validations are `token` presence/uniqueness and `refresh_token`
200	  uniqueness when used (l.17-18). No validation on `scopes`.
201	- `before_validation :generate_token, on: :create` (l.25) calls the configured
202	  generator (`UniqueToken.generate` → `SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)`, 43 chars) and
203	  stores `SHA256(plaintext)` because Redmine enables `hash_token_secrets`
204	  (`access_token_mixin.rb:472-478`, `secret_storing/sha256_hash.rb`). The plaintext
205	  is available once via `#plaintext_token` on the freshly created object.
206	- Lookup: `Doorkeeper::AccessToken.by_token(plain)` = `find_by_plaintext_token`
207	  (hashes, then `find_by`; `models/concerns/secret_storable.rb:42-47`). Verified: found.
208	- Expiry is **per row**: `expires_in` seconds relative to `created_at`
209	  (`models/concerns/expirable.rb`); `expired?`, `accessible?` (= not expired and not
210	  revoked), `revoke`, `revoked?` all work on an app-less token. Verified by back-dating
211	  `created_at`. The global `access_token_expires_in` only feeds the OAuth flows.
212	- A 43-char base64url token fails the legacy `Token.find_token` regex
213	  (`/\A[a-z0-9]+\z/i`), so a Doorkeeper token can never collide with or be looked up
214	  as a legacy API key. Verified: `Token.find_token('api', plain)` → nil.
215	- `Doorkeeper::Application.authorized_for(user)` selects distinct `application_id`
216	  from active tokens; app-less tokens do not appear on "Authorized applications".
217	  Verified: count 0.
218	- **HTTP, no code changes:** `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on `GET /users/current.json`
219	  → 200 through the existing branch (`application_controller.rb:134-138`); with scope
220	  `admin` the admin-only `GET /users.json` → 200. An expired token → 401 with
221	  `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="Redmine", error="invalid_token",
222	  error_description="The access token expired"` (Doorkeeper's error shape via
223	  `doorkeeper_render_error`, not Redmine's Basic realm).
224	- **Legacy transports do not reach Doorkeeper:** `X-Redmine-API-Key: <token>` → 401,
225	  Basic with token as username → 401. Two reasons: (1) Doorkeeper's default
226	  `access_token_methods` are `from_bearer_authorization`, `from_access_token_param`,
227	  `from_bearer_param` (`config.rb:586-591`); (2) in `find_current_user` the legacy
228	  branch `if (key = api_key_from_request)` wins whenever the header/param is present,
229	  and Doorkeeper sits in an `elsif`, so it is never consulted for those transports.
230	  Fixable: `Doorkeeper::OAuth::Token.from_request` accepts symbols **or callables**
231	  (`oauth/token.rb:7-13`), and `from_basic_authorization` (returns the Basic username,
232	  l.38-42) already exists; so `access_token_methods` can be configured in
233	  `config/initializers/30-redmine.rb` with two lambdas for the header and `?key=`
234	  plus `:from_basic_authorization`. The branch order in `find_current_user` must then
235	  become "legacy key lookup, and if that returns nil, Doorkeeper".
236	- Scopes: `scopes` is a space-separated string; `#scopes.all` returns an array.
237	  Redmine sets `user.oauth_scope = scopes.all.map(&:to_sym)`. With an **empty** scope
238	  list `Role#allowed_permissions([])` is unrestricted (`scope.present?` is false,
239	  `role.rb:304-311`) **but** `User#admin?` becomes false (`user.rb:737-739`), i.e. a
240	  blank-scope token would silently drop admin. A "full access" PAT therefore needs
241	  either the full enumerated scope list (frozen at creation; permissions added later
242	  by plugins would be missing) or a special case that skips `oauth_scope=` for
243	  app-less tokens with blank scopes (Bogdan Egikov's "blank = full access").
244	- `users/show.api.rsb:14` hides `api_key` from a non-admin user authenticated via
245	  OAuth (`authorized_by_oauth?`); a scoped PAT inherits that.
246	- **Pre-existing gap:** `oauth_access_tokens.resource_owner_id` has a foreign key to
247	  `users` (`20250611092155_create_doorkeeper_tables.rb:62-66`) and
248	  `User#remove_references_before_destroy` (`user.rb:971-993`) does not delete
249	  Doorkeeper rows. Verified on PostgreSQL: destroying a user who has any access token
250	  raises `ActiveRecord::InvalidForeignKey`. Any design that stores PATs in this table
251	  must delete them there (one line), which also fixes it for OAuth tokens.
252	- Subclassing: `Doorkeeper::AccessToken` is a plain `ActiveRecord::Base` subclass
253	  including a mixin (`orm/active_record/access_token.rb`). The table has no `type`
254	  column, so a `PersonalAccessToken < Doorkeeper::AccessToken` subclass shares the
255	  table without STI and can carry its own validations and scope
256	  (`where(application_id: nil)`); Doorkeeper's own lookup still instantiates the base
257	  class. Extra columns (`name`, `last_used_at`, suffix) are added by a Redmine
258	  migration; the app owns the schema of these tables.
259	
260	### 1.4 My account
261	
262	- `app/controllers/my_controller.rb`: `before_action :require_login`,
263	  `accept_api_auth :account` (l.26), `require_sudo_mode :account, only: :put` and
264	  `require_sudo_mode :reset_atom_key, :reset_api_key, :show_api_key, :destroy` (l.28-29).
265	  `show_api_key` (l.134) just sets `@user`; `reset_api_key` (l.139-149) destroys the
266	  existing `api` token, calls `User.current.api_key` to regenerate, flashes
267	  `notice_api_access_key_reseted`, redirects to `my_account_path`.
268	- Routes (`config/routes.rb:92-100`): `match 'my/account'` (get/put), `get 'my/api_key'`
269	  → `show_api_key` as `my_api_key`, `post 'my/api_key'` → `reset_api_key`,
270	  `post 'my/atom_key'`, `match 'my/password'`, `my/account/destroy`. All `my/*` routes are
271	  declared by hand (no `resources`), and `MyController` is a single controller with
272	  `self.main_menu = false`.
273	- Views (`app/views/my/`): `account.html.erb` is a two-column `labelled_form_for :user`
274	  with a `.contextual` bar (change password, OAuth authorized applications, hook
275	  `view_my_account_contextual`) and hooks `view_my_account`, `view_my_account_preferences`.
276	  The right sidebar is `content_for :sidebar` → `_sidebar.html.erb`, which renders the
277	  Atom key block and, if `Setting.rest_api_enabled?`, the "API access key" block: Show
278	  link (`remote: true`, served by `show_api_key.js.erb` which injects `@user.api_key`
279	  into `<pre id="api-access-key">`), a copy button (Stimulus `api-key-copy` controller,
280	  `test/system/api_key_copy_test.rb`), "created N ago" text and a Reset link (POST).
281	  `show_api_key.html.erb` is the non-JS fallback page. `account.api.rsb` exposes
282	  `api_key` in `GET /my/account.json`.
283	- Sudo mode (`lib/redmine/sudo_mode.rb`): `require_sudo_mode` class method (l.182-187)
284	  installs a `SudoRequestFilter` before_action; the filter **skips API requests**
285	  (l.158-159, `test_sudo_mode_should_skip_api_requests`) and is a no-op unless
286	  `Redmine::Configuration['sudo_mode']` is truthy (`enabled?`, l.232; **off by default**,
287	  see `config/configuration.yml.example:165-171`) and the user is logged in. Timeout
288	  `sudo_mode_timeout` minutes, default 15 (l.237-240). When active it re-renders
289	  `sudo_mode/new` with the original params as hidden fields. `test/test_helper.rb:40`
290	  calls `Redmine::SudoMode.disable!` globally; `test/integration/sudo_mode_test.rb`
291	  re-enables it per test. So "sudo-protected" in a spec means: declare it with
292	  `require_sudo_mode`, and it only bites when an admin turned sudo mode on.
293	- Menus: `Redmine::MenuManager` (`lib/redmine/menu_manager.rb`), maps defined in
294	  `lib/redmine/preparation.rb` (`:top_menu` l.164, `:account_menu` l.175 with
295	  `:my_account`, `:admin_menu` l.242). `menu_item :id, :only => [...]` at controller
296	  level selects the highlighted item (`menu_manager.rb:46-53`). The My account sidebar
297	  is not a menu; it is the `_sidebar.html.erb` partial.
298	
299	### 1.5 Settings
300	
301	- Declared in `config/settings.yml` (one YAML key per setting, options: `default`,
302	  `format: int`, `serialized: true`, `security_notifications: 1`). Examples relevant to
303	  us: `rest_api_enabled` (l.333, default 0), `jsonp_enabled` (l.336), `password_max_age`
304	  (l.54, `format: int`, default 0 = disabled; the "0 means off" idiom), `autologin`
305	  (l.167, int days), `session_lifetime`/`session_timeout` (l.67-75, minutes),
306	  `login_required`, `twofa`.
307	- `app/models/setting.rb`: `load_available_settings` (l.322) reads the YAML at class load
308	  and calls `define_setting` (l.303-320), which generates `Setting.xxx`,
309	  `Setting.xxx?` (= `to_i > 0`) and `Setting.xxx=`. Values are cached per process and
310	  `Setting.check_cache` runs each request (`application_controller.rb:104`).
311	  `Setting.set_all_from_params` (l.137) validates via `validate_all_from_params` (l.161)
312	  and sends security notifications for settings flagged `security_notifications`.
313	- Admin UI: `SettingsController#edit` (`app/controllers/settings_controller.rb:36-62`,
314	  `require_admin`, `require_sudo_mode :index, :edit, :plugin`), tabs from
315	  `SettingsHelper#administration_settings_tabs` (`app/helpers/settings_helper.rb:21-42`),
316	  partials in `app/views/settings/_*.html.erb`. The "API" tab is
317	  `app/views/settings/_api.html.erb` (two check boxes, `form_tag({:action => 'edit',
318	  :tab => 'api'})`). Helpers: `setting_check_box`, `setting_text_field`,
319	  `setting_select` etc. (`settings_helper.rb:58-113`). Labels come from
320	  `setting_<name>` keys in `en.yml` (e.g. `setting_rest_api_enabled`, l.492).
321	- Tests use `with_settings(rest_api_enabled: 1) { ... }` (`test/test_helper.rb:97`) or
322	  assign `Setting.rest_api_enabled = '1'` directly.
323	- `Redmine::Configuration` (`lib/redmine/configuration.rb`) is the separate
324	  `config/configuration.yml` layer (sudo mode, secret token, cookie names); not the
325	  place for per-installation feature settings.
326	
327	### 1.6 Tests
328	
329	- Layout (`test/`): `unit/` (models and `unit/lib/redmine/*`), `functional/`
330	  (controller tests, `Redmine::ControllerTest`), `integration/` (Rails integration
331	  tests, `Redmine::IntegrationTest`), `integration/api_test/` (one file per API resource,
332	  `Redmine::ApiTest::Base`), `integration/routing/`, `system/` (Capybara),
333	  `fixtures/`, `helpers/`, `test_helper.rb`, `object_helpers.rb` (`User.generate!`
334	  etc.). Minitest, fixtures are loaded per class with `fixtures :users, :tokens, ...`.
335	- `test/test_helper.rb`:
336	  - `Redmine::IntegrationTest#log_user(login, password)` (l.412) and
337	    `#credentials(user, password=nil)` (l.428) → `{'HTTP_AUTHORIZATION' => Basic ...}`
338	    (password defaults to the login).
339	  - `Redmine::ApiTest::Base` (l.437-444) sets `Setting.rest_api_enabled = '1'` in setup
340	    and back to `'0'` in teardown. `API_FORMATS = %w(json xml)`.
341	  - `with_settings` (l.97), `uploaded_test_file` (l.69).
342	- `test/integration/api_test/authentication_test.rb` is the reference for API auth
343	  behaviour: 401 + `WWW-Authenticate` without credentials; Basic username/password;
344	  Basic refused when 2FA active; API key as Basic username; `?key=`;
345	  `X-Redmine-API-Key`; wrong-action token refused; non-Basic `Authorization` header
346	  ignored; invalid UTF-8; session not used; `X-Redmine-Switch-User`. All use
347	  `GET /users/current.xml`. A PAT test file can mirror it exactly.
348	- `test/integration/api_test/disabled_rest_api_test.rb`: 403 for every credential type
349	  when `rest_api_enabled` is off.
350	- `test/functional/my_controller_test.rb`: logs in as user 2 (`jsmith`) in setup;
351	  `test_show_api_key`, `test_reset_api_key_*` at l.811-834.
352	- `test/integration/routing/my_test.rb` asserts the hand-written `my/*` routes.
353	- Fixtures: `users.yml` (`users_001` = `admin`/`admin`, id 1, admin; `users_002` =
354	  `jsmith`/`jsmith`, id 2; `users_005` = `dlopper2`, status 3 locked; `users_006` =
355	  anonymous, status 0), `tokens.yml` (2 rows, no `api` token). Password hashes are
356	  SHA1(salt+SHA1(password)) (`User#check_password?`, `user.rb:335-341`).
357	- `test/unit/lib/redmine/i18n_test.rb:206` `test_locales_validness` only checks every
358	  locale file loads; missing keys fall back to `en` (`config.i18n.fallbacks = true`,
359	  `config/application.rb:60`), so adding keys to `en.yml` only is sufficient for tests.
360	
361	### 1.7 Migrations and schema
362	
363	- Newest files in `db/migrate/` are `20250423065135_create_reactions.rb`,
364	  `20250530185658_ensure_wiki_tablesort_setting_is_stored_in_db.rb`,
365	  `20250611092155_create_doorkeeper_tables.rb`, `20250611092227_enable_pkce.rb`.
366	  Convention: `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_snake_case.rb`, `class X < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.2]`,
367	  `def change`, `t.references`/`add_index`/`add_foreign_key`, `t.timestamps null: false`
368	  where Rails-style timestamps are used (the old core tables use `created_on`/`updated_on`).
369	  Most 2024-2025 migrations have no `# frozen_string_literal` header (only
370	  `enable_pkce.rb` does), and no license header.
371	- `db/schema.rb` is **not** committed (`.gitignore:20`); `db/` only has `migrate/`.
372	  Reviewers verify with `bin/rails db:migrate`.
373	- Redmine supports MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite; migrations sometimes branch on
374	  `Redmine::Database.mysql?` (`20241103150135_change_settings_value_limit.rb`).
375	
376	### 1.8 #44371 (filtering `key` from logs)
377	
378	- `config/application.rb:68`: `config.filter_parameters += [:password]` is the only
379	  filter. There is no `config/initializers/filter_parameter_logging.rb`. Nothing in 6.1.2
380	  filters `key`, `X-Redmine-API-Key` or `access_token`. A PAT sent via `?key=` would be
381	  logged in plaintext by Rails' request log today; upstream is handling this separately
382	  (#44371), so we should not duplicate it but the README can mention it as a known
383	  limitation of `?key=` transport.
384	
385	### 1.9 i18n
386	
387	- All English strings are in `config/locales/en.yml` (flat keys under `en:`).
388	  Blocks by prefix (first occurrence; later additions are appended at the end of the
389	  file, l.1418-1461, regardless of prefix): `notice_*` (flash messages, l.160-201),
390	  `field_*` (model attribute labels, from l.285: `field_name` l.285, `field_created_on`
391	  l.297, `field_login` l.329, `field_last_login_on` l.332), `setting_*` (from l.433,
392	  `setting_rest_api_enabled` l.492), `label_*` (from l.628; `label_api_access_key`
393	  l.1030, `label_api` l.1127, `label_oauth_*` l.1171), `button_*` (l.1181-1245,
394	  `button_delete` l.1188, `button_create` l.1189), `text_*` (from l.1262,
395	  `text_are_you_sure` l.1279).
396	- ActiveRecord attribute names in `errors.full_messages` resolve through
397	  `ApplicationRecord.human_attribute_name` (`app/models/application_record.rb:23-32`),
398	  which tries `field_<model>_<attr>` then `field_<attr>` (strips `_id`). So a new
399	  model's attributes need `field_*` keys, e.g. `field_expires_at`, or the existing
400	  `field_name` is reused automatically.
401	- `lib/tasks/locales.rake`: `rake locales` = `locales:update` (adds new top-level
402	  `en.yml` keys to every other locale file, copying the English text) +
403	  `locales:check_interpolation`. Also `locales:add_key`, `locales:remove_key`,
404	  `locales:dup`. Core commits usually add keys only to `en.yml` (other locales fall
405	  back), so we do not need to touch the other 50 files.
406	
407	### 1.10 Other things a PAT design must respect
408	
409	- `safe_attributes` (`lib/redmine/safe_attributes.rb:33-84`): the Redmine idiom for
410	  mass assignment; `model.safe_attributes = params[:model]` with optional
411	  `:if => lambda {|obj, user| ...}` guards. New models should declare
412	  `safe_attributes 'name', 'expires_at', ...` rather than use strong params.
413	- `User#allowed_to?` / `Redmine::AccessControl` (`lib/redmine/access_control.rb`):
414	  permissions are declared in `lib/redmine/preparation.rb` via
415	  `map.permission :name, {controller => [actions]}, :public => true, :read => true`.
416	  `Permission#public?` marks permissions everyone has; `public_permissions` are what
417	  Doorkeeper uses as `default_scopes`. API auth does not interact with permissions
418	  beyond setting `User.current`; authorization happens later in `authorize` /
419	  `authorize_global` (`application_controller.rb:322-342`).
420	- `users.status` (`app/models/principal.rb:24-27`): 0 anonymous, 1 active,
421	  2 registered, 3 locked. `User.active` scope and `Principal#active?` (l.146).
422	  `Token.find_active_user` and the OAuth branch both refuse non-active users, so a
423	  PAT lookup must do the same.
424	- 2FA: `User#twofa_active?` (l.398) blocks Basic username/password only; API keys
425	  bypass 2FA by design (this is the "2FA bypass" the ticket complains about).
426	  `User#must_activate_twofa?` (l.402) and `check_twofa_activation` are session-only
427	  redirects and never fire for API requests. `destroy_tokens` (l.962) wipes session,
428	  autologin and recovery tokens when 2FA is enabled, not API tokens.
429	- `User#must_change_password?` (l.367): only enforced for Basic auth (see 1.1). API-key
430	  auth ignores it; a PAT path that mirrors the header/param branch inherits that
431	  behaviour unless we decide otherwise.
432	- `User.current` is a thread-local set once per request; `user.oauth_scope=` is the only
433	  per-request mutable auth state, so a PAT can piggyback on it later for scopes.
434	- Doorkeeper admin screens require `Setting.rest_api_enabled?`; a PAT UI should follow
435	  the same gate (`_sidebar.html.erb:21` already hides the API key block when off).
436	- Hooks: `call_hook(:view_my_account_contextual)`, `:view_my_account`,
437	  `:view_my_account_preferences` exist for plugins, so adding a new block to the sidebar
438	  partial is the core way (not a hook).
439	- `Redmine::Utils.random_hex(n)` is the existing random-secret helper; `bcrypt` is
440	  already a dependency (used by Doorkeeper for application secrets) if a slow hash is
441	  wanted, but Doorkeeper itself uses SHA-256 for access tokens, which is the precedent
442	  for high-entropy tokens.
443	
444	## 2. What we built
445	
446	Status: **nothing yet**.
447	
448	For each component, once built: what it is, how it works, why it is shaped that way
449	(reference `D-NNN`), known limits. Suggested subsections:
450	
451	- Data model and migration
452	- Token generation, hashing, and lookup
453	- Authentication flow and legacy key coexistence
454	- My account UI
455	- Settings
456	- Tests
457	- Optional pillars (if any)
458	- Known limits and deferred work
459	
460	## 3. Workflow and tooling notes
461	
462	- Tool: Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1) with custom subagents in `.claude/agents/`.
463	- Raw transcripts live in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kbagaiev-Projects-TaxDome/` and
464	  are copied unedited into `ai-workflow/logs/` before submission.
465
